text: At a ceremony Thursday evening at the Tern Hall civic center, the Calder Vane Prize for architecture was awarded to Tomasz Okonjo, whose low-rise housing plan for the North Quay district impressed judges with what they called “careful scale and public warmth.” I was told by prize coordinator Leena Maris that Okonjo edged out three other finalists after a final review held yesterday. The announcement drew a modest crowd of architects, students and city officials, including Deputy Mayor Alaric Finn, who said the winning design “fits Baywater’s shoreline without showing off.” Okonjo accepted the prize with a short speech and thanked his team from the Marrow Street studio. The award carries a stipend of 18,000 sovereigns and a plaque displayed at Tern Hall.
